description: The mathematics and algorithms behind moving characters and crowds in games and film: skeletal animation, inverse kinematics, captured motion, blending, physics-based control and large-scale crowd models. Students implement each method in the lab, plot the results and judge how believable the motion looks.
modelledOn: Parent, Computer Animation: Algorithms and Techniques
Lengyel, Mathematics for 3D Game Programming and Computer Graphics
Millington, Artificial Intelligence for Games (movement chapters)
outcomes: Represent poses with quaternions and transform hierarchies, and skin a mesh to a skeleton with linear blend and dual quaternion methods.
Solve inverse kinematics problems with analytic, CCD, FABRIK and Jacobian methods and compare convergence and quality.
Clean, retarget and blend captured motion and combine clips with state machines and blend spaces.
Build a simple physics-based character controller with proportional-derivative joint control and balance reasoning.
Simulate crowds with flocking, velocity obstacles and social force models and relate them to measured pedestrian flow.
Design and run an evaluation of the believability of generated motion using objective metrics and a small perceptual study.

units.title: Skeletal animation and skinning
topics: Rotations in animation: Euler angles, gimbal lock, quaternions and spherical linear interpolation
Skeleton hierarchies, bind pose and forward kinematics with local and world transforms
Linear blend skinning, skinning weights and the candy-wrapper artefact
Dual quaternion skinning and corrective blend shapes
Keyframes and curves: linear, Catmull-Rom and Bezier interpolation, easing and curve editing

units.title: Inverse kinematics
topics: Analytic two-bone IK for arms and legs using the law of cosines
Cyclic coordinate descent and its convergence behaviour
FABRIK: forward and backward reaching for chains
Jacobian methods: pseudo-inverse, damped least squares and singularities
Joint limits, constraints, foot placement on uneven ground and look-at IK

units.title: Motion capture data and retargeting
topics: Capture technologies: marker-based optical, inertial suits and single-camera pose estimation from phone video
BVH and similar file formats; cleaning noise, filtering and gap filling
Retargeting motion between skeletons of different proportions
Time alignment and dynamic time warping of clips; motion editing
Root motion extraction and removing foot-skate

units.title: Animation blending and state machines
topics: Linear blending, additive animation and masks for upper and lower body
Blend trees and two-dimensional blend spaces for locomotion
Animation state machines, transitions, layers and cross-fades
Motion graphs and motion matching for responsive locomotion
Inertialisation and transition smoothing without cross-fade cost

units.title: Physics-based character control
topics: Rigid body dynamics for articulated figures; ragdolls and joint constraints
Proportional-derivative control of joints; gain tuning and stability
Balance: inverted pendulum models, centre of pressure and zero-moment point
Active ragdolls, hit reactions and blending between kinematic and simulated motion
Learning controllers: trajectory optimisation and reinforcement learning to imitate motion clips

units.title: Crowd steering and flocking models
topics: Boids: separation, alignment and cohesion; emergent flocking
Steering behaviours: seek, arrive, pursue, wander, obstacle avoidance and path following
Velocity obstacles, reciprocal velocity obstacles and ORCA collision avoidance
Social force model and its parameters
Navigation for crowds: navigation meshes, flow fields and potential fields

units.title: Crowd scale, density and behaviour
topics: Pedestrian dynamics: fundamental diagram, lane formation, bottlenecks and stop-and-go waves
Spatial hashing and parallel update for tens of thousands of agents
Rendering crowds: GPU skinning, instancing, level of detail and impostors
Group behaviour, roles and goals; emergency evacuation of a market or stadium
Calibrating a crowd model against video-derived trajectories

units.title: Evaluating believability and project
topics: Perceptual factors in motion: the uncanny valley, foot-skate visibility and timing thresholds
Objective motion metrics: pose error, jerk, smoothness, energy and collision counts
Designing a perceptual user study: stimuli, controls, rating scales and significance tests
Ablation and comparison of methods; reporting results with confidence intervals
Project: a character locomotion system plus a crowd scene, with an evaluation report

schedule.title: Rotations, hierarchies and skinning
schedule.exercise: Compose three joint rotations as quaternions, compute the world position of a fingertip through a four-bone arm, and explain the candy-wrapper artefact in a twisted forearm.

tasks.title: Rotate a vector by 90 degrees about two axes using Euler angles in both orders and compare with the quaternion product
Code forward kinematics for a 4-bone arm from local transforms and print the world position of the hand for five poses
Implement linear blend skinning for a bent tube with two bones, twist the elbow and measure how much the volume collapses

schedule.title: Better skinning and animation curves
schedule.exercise: Compare linear blend and dual quaternion skinning on a twisted limb, and design a keyframe curve for a bouncing ball with easing at the contacts.

tasks.title: Plot linear, Catmull-Rom and Bezier interpolation through six keyframes and note where each overshoots or looks stiff
Interpolate between two rotations with linear lerp and slerp over 20 steps and plot the angular speed of each
Implement dual quaternion skinning for the twisted tube and compare its volume and joint appearance with linear blend skinning

schedule.title: Solving inverse kinematics
schedule.exercise: Solve a 3-bone chain reaching a target with CCD, FABRIK and a damped least squares step, and compare the iterations each needs and what happens when the target is out of reach.

tasks.title: Solve a two-bone planar arm for ten targets using the law of cosines and plot both elbow-up and elbow-down solutions
Implement FABRIK for a 5-bone chain and report the iterations to reach within 1 cm for 20 random targets
Implement a Jacobian damped least squares solver and show behaviour near a singularity with and without the damping term

schedule.title: Motion capture data and retargeting
schedule.exercise: Take a noisy walking clip, filter and gap-fill it, retarget it to a shorter skeleton, and list where foot-skate appears and how to remove it.

tasks.title: Smooth a noisy joint-angle signal with a moving average and a low-pass filter and compare residual noise and lag
Align two walking clips of different lengths with dynamic time warping and show the warping path on the cost grid
Detect foot contacts in a clip from velocity and height, then fix the foot-skate with IK and report skating distance before and after

schedule.title: Blending clips and state machines
schedule.exercise: Design a locomotion state machine with idle, walk, run and jump, including the transition conditions and blend durations, and define a two-dimensional blend space for strafing.

tasks.title: Step through a character state machine with a given input sequence and record the state and blend weights at each frame
Blend walk and run clips by speed with a one-dimensional blend tree and check the foot phase stays synchronised across 100 speeds
Implement a nearest-neighbour motion matching search over a pose database and measure response latency to a change in desired direction

schedule.title: Ragdolls and joint control
schedule.exercise: Tune the stiffness and damping of a PD controller on a single hinge, then explain why a standing character needs its centre of pressure under the support polygon.

tasks.title: Simulate a single joint with a PD controller for ten gain pairs and plot step responses, marking overshoot and settling time
Simulate a three-link ragdoll falling onto the floor with joint limits and check the energy never rises between frames
Simulate a linear inverted pendulum, apply pushes of 20, 40 and 60 N, and find the ones recoverable by stepping to a new foot position

schedule.title: Active ragdolls and learned control
schedule.exercise: Describe how a character should blend from keyframed walking to ragdoll when hit, how to blend back, and how you would train a policy to imitate a clip.

tasks.title: Blend a keyframed pose and a simulated pose with a weight sweeping from 0 to 1 and plot joint angle error against the target pose
Train a small neural network on joint-angle targets from a recorded gait and watch the loss fall across 50 epochs in the visualiser
Use random search to tune PD gains of a two-link walker so it imitates a reference trajectory, and report the imitation error per generation

schedule.title: Flocking and steering
schedule.exercise: Implement the three boid rules for 200 agents, vary the weights, and describe which settings give a flock, a swarm and a scattered cloud.

tasks.title: Code boids with separation, alignment and cohesion for 100 agents and print the average nearest-neighbour distance every 50 steps
Add obstacle avoidance and path following to steering agents so 50 agents cross a field with 5 obstacles with zero collisions
Implement ORCA-style avoidance for 40 agents swapping positions on a circle and compare collisions and travel time with simple repulsion

schedule.title: Social forces and crowd navigation
schedule.exercise: Describe the three terms of the social force model, and compare navigation with a flow field against individual path finding for 5,000 agents heading to one exit.

tasks.title: Run A* on a navigation grid with obstacles for three start points and record nodes expanded and path length
Compute a flow field from a goal using breadth-first search and move 500 agents along it, counting steps to reach the exit
Implement the social force model for 100 agents in a corridor and tune parameters until two opposing streams form lanes

schedule.title: Pedestrian dynamics and scaling up
schedule.exercise: Measure flow against density in your simulated corridor, draw the fundamental diagram, and explain how spatial hashing reduces neighbour search cost from quadratic to linear.

tasks.title: Plot speed against density from a table of corridor measurements and fit a line to find the jam density
Add a spatial hash grid to a crowd of 10,000 agents and compare neighbour search time against brute force
Simulate a 1 m wide door with 300 agents, measure the flow rate and reproduce the faster-is-slower effect by raising desired speed

schedule.title: Crowd behaviour, evacuation and calibration
schedule.exercise: Plan an evacuation drill model for a market with three exits, and describe how to calibrate agent speeds from trajectories extracted from a phone video.

tasks.title: Simulate 200 agents evacuating a room with two exits and report the evacuation time and per-exit usage
Fit a mean and standard deviation for walking speed from 40 extracted trajectories and sample agent speeds from the fitted distribution
Compare evacuation time for a market with exits blocked at random and propose the one widening that reduces the 95th percentile the most

schedule.title: Measuring motion quality
schedule.exercise: Pick five objective metrics for a locomotion system, define a rating-scale study with two methods and twenty clips, and state the statistical test you would use.

tasks.title: Compute jerk, smoothness and pose error for two motion clips and tabulate which clip scores better on each metric
Analyse ratings from 20 participants for two methods using a paired test and report the p-value and effect size
Plot rating against foot-skate distance from the given study data and estimate the threshold at which half of the viewers notice it

schedule.title: Project evaluation and reporting
schedule.exercise: Present your locomotion and crowd project with a comparison table, error bars and a candid account of where the motion still looks wrong.

tasks.title: Compute the mean and a 95 percent confidence interval of a motion metric over 30 clips and plot it with error bars
Run an ablation that turns off IK foot correction, blending and PD control in turn and tabulate the change in each metric
Run your complete locomotion controller with a 2,000-agent crowd scene, report frame time and quality metrics, and defend one trade-off you made
